title: Nashville council moves to require food trucks to vacate lots after three-day runs
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
Nashville council moves to require food trucks to vacate lots after three-day runs
Council members said the town's food truck ordinance was ambiguous enough that a truck could sit on a private lot indefinitely as long as it closed every fourth day, prompting a planned amendment to require it to physically leave the property.
The Nashville Town Council discussed amending its food truck ordinance during a meeting Thursday, October 1, 2026, after a resident inquiry exposed ambiguity over how long a truck could stay parked on private property.
THE AMBIGUITY Under the current ordinance, food trucks may operate for three consecutive days before closing, but the rule does not specify that the truck itself must move. A council member explained the loophole: "It says three days, but that it has to be closed, but it doesn't say it's supposed to be closed."
One council member described the scenario driving the question: "If the part if the property owner is okay with it, parking lot owner is okay with it, that food truck could sit there, open three days, close for a day, open three days, close."
THE CONCERN Members said they never intended the ordinance to allow a permanent fixture. "I certainly didn't intend for it to become a permanent thing," one member said. Another warned of consequences if the rule isn't tightened: "there's going to be a lot of push back if we if we don't require them to move it."
THE FIX The council discussed an amendment requiring the truck to leave the tax parcel after three days rather than simply closing its doors, while still allowing it to operate Friday, Saturday and Sunday and return the following week. One member said the change "discourages some bad behavior."
WHAT'S NEXT The amendment is intended to clarify existing intent rather than change it, members said, and will be brought up at the council's next meeting. A draft has already been sent to Sandy for the permit application.
